newsitem.title: USA: US T-bond up full point on retail sales declines.
newsitem.headline: US T-bond up full point on retail sales declines.

text.p: The benchmark U.S. Treasury bond was up a full point after the U.S. Commerce Department reported that retail sales slipped in May and fell even more than first reported in April.

The government said U.S. retail sales slipped 0.1 percent in May, a more subdued trend than the modest 0.4 percent increase economists had forecast. Without auto sales, the retail sales figure was also down 0.1 percent, again more depressed than the moderate 0.3 percent rise analysts had anticipated.

Reinforcing the impression of weakness in the retail sector, the Commerce Department also revised the April sales decline to 0.9 percent from the 0.3 percent originally reported. It was the biggest drop since February 1995, when sales fell 1.6 percent.
Excluding auto transactions, retail sales fell 0.5 percent in April, a steeper fall than the 0.1 percent decline originally reported.

The Labor Department's weekly jobless claims report did nothing to lessen the impact of the retail sales data, analysts said. Contrary to expectations, which were for jobless claims to drop to 326,000 after a surge to 337,000 in the prior week, claims edged up to 339,000 in the week ended June 7 from a revised 338,000 a week earlier.
